source.title: Localizing Persona Representations in LLMs
source.authors: C. Cintas; M. Rateike; Erik Miehling; Elizabeth Daly; Skyler Speakman

page_placements.theme: Residual-stream and embedding basis dimensions (not MLP neurons) mix concepts

record.tranche_reason: Measures overlap among salient activation coordinates for persona representations in language models, using Deep Scan rather than the original sources’ neuron-level methods.
record.gate_note: The study measures shared salient activation coordinates across persona categories, not MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts. Its overlap results are retained as bearing on V2 because the authors explicitly interpret shared activations across personas as polysemy. The layer-separation and detection precision/recall results are not rows: they do not measure polysemantic overlap. The study also does not identify whether overlapping activations encode a common feature.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It measures overlap of Deep Scan salient coordinates in Llama3's last-layer, last-token residual vector across personas of the same topic. These are related concepts, not unrelated inputs. The coordinates are not MLP neurons, and no neuron is shown to respond to unrelated tokens or contexts. The authors label the overlap polysemanticity, but that is their interpretation of a related construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that ethical views 'show greater polysemantic overlap', interpreting shared salient activations as polysemy. Political views appear more distinctly localized. The work is correlational, and causal editing is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PCA-based layer analysis and Deep Scan on last-token embedding coordinates for persona statements; it does not use the original sources’ vision-neuron analysis or SoLU method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported overlap varies by persona topic. The overlap analysis is limited to Llama3’s last layer; the separate layer-separation analysis finds differences by layer and model but does not measure polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama3-8B-Instruct's last-layer last-token vector, 17.55% of coordinates are salient for all ethical personas. The shares are 9.42% for political and 7.62% for personality personas. Topic-level overlaps are 0–12%. No chance baseline is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Salient residual-stream coordinates for related persona concepts overlap more for ethical than for political personas.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Eighth AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES2025)
record.problems: Overlap is measured only in Llama3’s last-layer last-token embedding coordinates and does not establish that individual MLP neurons respond to unrelated inputs. The authors note that the dataset is LLM-generated, English-only, and primarily reflects WEIRD perspectives, with political views centered largely on U.S. politics. The analysis is correlational and does not test whether identified activations causally generate personas.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying overlap results were left out. Q1 layer-separation metrics and the precision/recall validation tables were not recorded as rows because they measure separability or detection performance, not polysemantic overlap.

untested.parts: No MLP neuron analysis, no responses to unrelated tokens or contexts, and no comparison across layers of polysemantic share.
No test of initialization, regularization or training noise.
No variation of architecture or activation function bearing on polysemanticity.
Does not test whether overlaps reflect one shared feature; the authors only speculate about shared conceptual features.
Does not vary activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V2 labels are rejected. Salient set sizes (Tab. 4: about 1170–1210 at layer 31; Tab. 8: 1721–2692) are large relative to 4096, so the reported intersections lack a random-overlap baseline. The units are residual-stream dimensions, which have no privileged basis, not neurons.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures last-token embedding activation coordinates, not MLP neurons specifically; it does not measure a large share of all neurons, token-level responses generally, or variation in polysemanticity across layers. Overlap is tested only in Llama3’s last layer.
No capacity-pressure or superposition mechanism is tested.
No initialization, regularization, or training-noise mechanism is tested.

The study compares representation separation across model families, but does not test changes in polysemantic-neuron share due to architecture, activation functions, or regularization, nor performance costs of reducing it.
The study does not investigate whether apparent mixtures resolve into a shared feature or related jobs.
It does not vary activation range or explanation scoring to test how those choices change polysemanticity measurements.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap of Deep Scan salient activation coordinates across ethical personas in last-layer last-token representations.
rows.measure: Shared salient activations as a percentage and count of the 4096-dimensional embedding vector
rows.note: The authors characterize this as substantial overlap and interpret it as polysemanticity across ethical representations.
rows.check: Overlap of salient residual-stream coordinates across related ethical personas is not MLP neurons responding to unrelated inputs. There is no chance-overlap baseline, and the salient sets are large (|OS*| about 1100–2700 of 4096, Tab. 4/8), so chance overlap may be substantial.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Authors explicitly link the overlaps to polysemanticity and call ethical views 'polysemous', but do not test the neuron claim or use it as a tool.

tranche.reason: Measures overlap of Deep Scan salient coordinates of the last-layer last-token hidden vector across related personas of one topic; not MLP neurons responding to unrelated inputs, so no version is tested.

source_check.notes: All four rows match the text. Layer 31 is Llama3's last layer of 32. The authors' 'polysemantic' reading applies to residual-stream coordinates shared across related personas, not to neurons. The work is correlational and has no chance-overlap baseline. The T6/discusses call stands.

statements.correction: Text: Llama3 last-layer last-token vector (4096 dims), Deep Scan salient activations shared across all personas of a topic: Ethics 17.55% (719), Politics 9.42% (386), Personality 7.62% (312). No chance-overlap baseline is given.
